text: Many people find pleasure in cultivating gardens, as this practice supports soil quality, increases visual appeal, and promotes personal health. Successful cultivation relies heavily on two key components: mulch and compost. Mulch holds moisture in place and stops weeds from growing, whereas compost supplies essential nutrients to the ground. These materials are vital for a sound ecosystem yet frequently ignored. Using mulch limits erosion, wards off pests and illness, and improves soil through organic matter, all of which lead to better yields. Conversely, compost strengthens soil vitality, raising fertility and resistance so that vegetation, helpful insects, and microscopic life thrive. When gardeners apply both substances, they establish a lasting and productive setting for their crops.
